scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: URGENT!! Both halves of the campus are OFF THE NETWORK
-- nobody on either side can reach their gateway thingies. This all started
after "a reload". Something around the big switch must be wrong, but I don't
know what. Could someone look at it and get both floors online again!!!
Thanks!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified gateway reachability from every VLAN, and all default gateways are up and responding normally. Examples: pc1 (10.5.0.1) successfully pings its gateway 10.5.0.254 (0% loss, ~1.4 ms). pc3 (10.6.0.3) reaches 10.6.0.254 (0% loss, ~2.1 ms). VLAN 10 hosts (pc5/6/7/8) reach 172.16.10.254 (0% loss, ~2 ms). VLAN 20 hosts (pc9/10/11) reach 172.16.20.254 (0% loss, ~1.8–2.0 ms). VLAN 30 hosts (pc12/13/14) reach 172.16.30.254 (0% loss, ~1.6–2.2 ms). The topology-wide probe also shows cross-VLAN connectivity to 172.16.10.x hosts from all other segments with normal RTTs. Client routing tables confirm correct default routes to the .254 gateways in each subnet.

Mechanism and localization: If there was an outage “after a reload,” it was transient while the core/aggregation came back up; however, at present the Layer-3 SVI gateways and the uplinks through the “big switch” (mswitch0 and attached switches) are operating normally, as evidenced by consistent gateway ICMP reachability and no packet loss.

Root cause: No persistent fault found; likely a brief post-reload convergence/startup gap that has already cleared.

Corrective fix: No changes required. If users still report issues, have them retry/flush ARP or renew DHCP and verify they’re on the correct VLAN port. From the network side, all gateways and inter-VLAN paths are healthy now.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly shows pc1->10.5.0.254 and pc3->10.6.0.254 pings with 0% loss, confirming the sshswitch SVIs are up at baseline.

The investigation log shows repeated successful pings from hosts in each VLAN to their .254 gateways and host interfaces up, which supports the agent's conclusion that the SVIs/gateways are functioning. One minor claim in the writeup (explicit client routing-table prints) is not shown in the log, but the core diagnosis follows logically from the observed reachability tests and probes.
